title: Hosted tier SLIs: define canonical availability/error/streaming disconnect metrics + docs
creator: Rafael Mendes
project: Tiered SLO definitions + error budget policy
description:
Goal: Define Hosted-tier SLIs (availability, error rate, latency, streaming disconnects) and implement canonical metric definitions across gateway -> routing -> runtime so SLO/budget calculations are consistent across regions/models/routes.

This ticket covers:
- Final SLI definitions for Hosted tier (what counts as success/failure, which codes are excluded, how streaming is measured).
- Canonical metric names + labels, including tier propagation and guardrails for cardinality.
- Reference queries/recording rules for SLI computation used by slo-toolkit + dashboards.

Out of scope:
- Dedicated pool readiness SLIs (tracked in ENG-2419).
- Error budget policy + enforcement (ENG-2420/2422/2427).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Hosted tier SLI definitions are published and linked from the tiered SLO page, including explicit exclusions (invalid auth, malformed requests, customer-side timeouts) and examples.
2) Canonical metrics are emitted with consistent semantics across gateway/routing/runtime and include tier=hosted dimension.
3) Streaming disconnect taxonomy is implemented in gateway metrics (client abort vs server-side disconnect) and is queryable per route/model/region without exceeding cardinality budget.
4) SLI queries used by dashboards and slo-toolkit produce matching results (+/- 0.1%) when validated against sampled logs for at least 3 regions and top 10 routes.
5) Backward compatibility: existing dashboards/alerts continue to function during rollout (dual-write or aliasing where needed) with a documented deprecation plan.
implementation_notes:
Hosted SLIs (proposed canonical definitions):
- Availability (non-streaming): successful if HTTP 2xx/3xx and request reached model execution; failure if 5xx, gateway timeout, upstream timeout, or runtime error. Exclusions: 4xx (except 408/429 depending on classification), invalid auth (401/403), invalid params (400/422), customer-canceled requests when clearly attributable (see streaming).
- Error rate: focus on server-attributed failures: 5xx + timeouts + capacity/overload rejections that are Redwood-controlled (e.g., 503 due to internal protect mode). Track 429 separately as a quota SLI (not counted against availability by default).
- Streaming disconnect rate: count streams that terminate before sending a terminal completion event. Classify into:
  (a) client_abort (client closed connection / explicit cancel)
  (b) server_disconnect (gateway/routing/runtime closed unexpectedly)
  (c) upstream_timeout (no token progress for N seconds)
  (d) transport_error (LB reset, TLS error)
  SLI is primarily server_disconnect + upstream_timeout; client_abort is excluded from failure count.
- Latency (Hosted): for streaming endpoints, track TTFT (time-to-first-token) as the primary latency SLI; overall stream duration reported separately for diagnostics.

Metric conventions:
- Required labels (bounded): tier, region, route, model_family, status_class, error_class, streaming=true/false.
- Avoid unbounded labels: raw model_id, customer_id, prompt_id, user_agent, error_message.
- Provide mapping layer in gateway for route normalization (e.g., /v1/chat/completions and /v1/completions) to reduce label churn.

Validation:
- Compare metric-derived SLI numerators/denominators against sampled request logs (Nadia + Caleb) for top routes in us-east-1, eu-west-1, us-west-2.
- Specifically validate treatment of 499 and client cancel: ensure excluded from failure unless server-side disconnect is detected.

Docs:
- Confluence pages to update/link:
  - Tiered SLO definitions (Hosted vs Dedicated)
  - SLI spec: success/timeouts/streaming disconnects
  - Dashboard naming/structure for SLO views
rollout_plan:
Phase A (1 week): Implement/dual-write canonical counters in gateway + routing + runtime; keep existing metrics as-is. Validate cardinality and sampling.
Phase B (1 week): Switch dashboard queries to canonical recording rules (warn-only on alerting thresholds). Monitor diffs.
Phase C (1 week): Cut over slo-toolkit config for Hosted tier and begin using canonical SLIs for burn-rate alerts (still warn-only gates). Announce deprecation timeline for old metrics.
Phase D: Remove/stop emitting deprecated metrics after 2 stable weeks and after SRE sign-off.
